claim_adjudications.span: the top line, gross profit, the rounded company-reported GAAP gross margin, the company-reported processing-volume operating metric, and the company-defined Adjusted EBITDA all moved higher
total operating expenses rose by more than gross profit did, with the largest single-step increase appearing in other operating expenses, and the operating loss widened accordingly
Other income, net declined, so it absorbed less of the operating shortfall, and the pretax loss widened further; the GAAP net loss widened again after a larger income tax expense
The Adjusted EBITDA increase is a company-defined non-GAAP measure from a reconciliation table and is not comparable line-for-line with the GAAP operating loss
The gross margin figures are company-reported rounded percentages, so the displayed step is a rounded percentage-point difference and not a precise margin computation
Research state is held pending a complete filing review covering the non-GAAP reconciliation, the composition of other operating expenses, and management guidance

notes: Correctly separates TPV from revenue, rounded GAAP gross margin from precise arithmetic, and adjusted EBITDA from GAAP losses. The selected-row operating and below-line bridge is accurate; unexplained expense and non-GAAP divergence are held rather than turned into an unsupported positive decision.
